chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He (the Imam) said to me: 'O Ziyad! What would you say if we were to issue a fatwa to a man from those who follow our authority, with something from taqiyya?'
He (Abu Ubayda) said: I said to him (the Imam): 'You are more knowing, may I be sacrificed for you.'
He (the Imam) said: 'If he acts upon it, it is better for him and of greater reward.'
And in another report: 'If he acts upon it, he will be rewarded; and if he abandons it, by God, he sins.'

key_terms.أَثِمَ: He sins — incurs spiritual sin for abandoning the Imam's directive
key_terms.أَفْتَيْنَا: We issued a fatwa — legal ruling; the plural 'we' is the royal/majestic plural used by the Imam
key_terms.أُوجِرَ: He will be rewarded — rewarded by God for compliance with the Imam's guidance
key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Taqiyya — precautionary dissimulation; a legal practice in Shia jurisprudence permitting concealment of one's true beliefs or practices under duress or danger
key_terms.يَتَوَلَّانَا: Those who follow our authority (wilaya) — Shia believers who accept the Imam's religious and political guardianship

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about the reward for following taqiyya in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) discusses with his companion Abu Ubayda the ruling on taqiyya (precautionary dissimulation), affirming that acting upon a fatwa issued under taqiyya brings reward, while abandoning it constitutes a sin. This hadith appears in the chapter on 'Differences in the Hadith' (Chapter 21), addressing the legitimacy of legal opinions given under conditions of taqiyya. The chapter context suggests that the hadith itself may be an example of the very variance in narration that the chapter explores, as two slightly different versions of the Imam's statement are preserved side by side.
